messages:
anna: quick heads-up — ran the tengu-int4 canary against the funcall suite and saw a ~2.3% bump in parse failures vs baseline. reproducer attached below.

mike: ugh. same spike here on my run, looks like suffix padding is greedy and stomps closing brace sometimes.

sasha: can you paste the raw model output? wanna see whether it's truncated or has stray tokens.

anna: here's one of the failing outputs (copied raw from canary logs):
```
{
  "action": "create_issue",
  "args": {
    "title": "Crash on save",
    "body": "Steps to repro..."
  }
} }
 



```
anna: note the extra space+brace and a control char ( ) appended after the JSON. parser rejects it.

liam: that control char looks like a tokenization artifact — maybe the tokenizer emits a page-break control on some quant kernels? seen something similar with older int8 kernels.

mike: also seeing cases where the model emits an extra trailing comma: `},
}` — strict json lint fails. seems specific to tempering and sampling config used in the canary.

anna: current canary config: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.95, penalty=None, decode_cutoff=4096, kv_cache=true, continuous_batching=on. 

anna: hypothesis: quant decoder + small beam-ish variations introduces non-deterministic suffix bytes. fallback policy currently retries up to 2x with the same model variant then falls back to non-quantized mirror. but retry doesn't help because output is syntactically wrong, not missing.

sasha: quick mitigation idea: run a preparse sanitizer that strips trailing control chars and collapses extra braces heuristically, but we should treat as a canary detector not permanent. canary-bot: flag run id 2026-07-10T10:18Z has parse_failure_rate 2.3% (+1.7% vs baseline).

canary-bot: detector: structured-parse-failure; affected-sample-count: 23; total-samples: 1000; severity: medium; suggested-action: collect seed prompts + raw tokens.

liam: we should collect the raw token ids for failing samples (before detokenize). hard to root without token stream. canary infra: can we enable token logging for a small subset?

mike: yes, canary infra can toggle token debug for 50 samples max. i'll flip it on for the next run.

anna: plan proposal: 1) run token-debug subset (mike will flip), 2) add a post-output sanitizer for canary that removes Unicode control chars and trims repeated closing braces, 3) re-run with decode_cutoff and an `eos_penalty=+2` to discourage stray control tokens, 4) if still failing escalate to runtime/quant team.

sasha: add a quick eval: run the same prompts against tengu-fp16 mirror and compute diff of final tokens for failing examples — helps see whether generator diverges near EOS.

liam: also try small change: set `remove_suffix_newlines=true` and `max_newline_runs=1` in the decoding config to avoid long newline sequences that confuse parser.

anna: noted. mike — please collect token dumps and paste 3 representative diffs here when ready. i'll add the sanitizer patch to canary harness (only enabled for the next 24h).

mike: will do. flipping token-debug now. run kicking off in ~2m.

canary-bot: run 1768524680-20260710 token-debug enabled (sample cap 50).

anna: thanks — if we confirm it's quant decoder noise we'll propose a canary rollback for the quant build and block wider rollout.

sasha: one more ask — add the parser error class to telemetry (trailing_control_char / extra_closing_brace / trailing_comma) so we can split by error mode.

anna: good call. logging ticket created: INF-1142. attaching checklist: postmortem if >1% persists after sanitizer + eos_penalty.

liam: thumbs-up. small note: keep the fp16 mirror in the pipeline for quick compare runs; reduces noise in root cause.

mike: pasted token diff for sample #17:
```
fp16 tokens: [102, 4321, 77, 9, 2] -> decodes to ' }'
int4 tokens: [102, 4321, 77, 9, 2, 12, 7] -> decodes to ' } } '
```

mike: so int4 appended two extra tokens (one is control). looks like quant kernel produced extra decode steps past EOS.

anna: thanks — copying this into INF-1142. if teams agree, next steps are rollback candidate + deeper quant kernel audit.

sasha: I'll start a tiny mutation test to see if adding `eos_token_override` fixes the odd tail.

anna: ok wrapping up here. summary: token-debug enabled, sanitizer + telemetry landed to canary harness, investigating quant decoder tailing. will update thread after next run. :eyes:
